title: gpu-nsight-occupancy-analysis-2026-03-18
content:
Context and purpose:
Ran a set of Nsight profiling runs to understand low GPU SM occupancy and suboptimal token-per-second for the 8k-context streaming path on H100s. Goal was to identify kernel-level bottlenecks (compute vs memory vs scheduler stalls), evaluate CUDA Graph capture effectiveness, and propose immediate mitigations for the canary workload.

Environment and config:
- Model: open-llm-3B (decoder-only), mixed-precision int8 quant, KV-cache enabled
- Serving runtime: rwd-serve v1.12.4 (custom CUDA kernels for attention + rotary)
- Hardware: 8x NVIDIA H100 (p52) per node, PCIe attach on test rig
- Nsight suite: Nsight Systems 2025.4 + Nsight Compute 2025.3
- Capture modes: nv-nsight-cu-cli (kernel metrics) + nsys timeline (system + API)
- Workload: steady-state stream at target concurrency 12, seq length 1024 generate-to-end (avg 128 tokens)
- CUDA Graph: tested both dynamic launch and per-batch static capture

Commands used (notes):
- nsight-sys: nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --output=run-2026-03-18.nsys-rep --duration=120 --sample=none 
- ncu: ncu --metrics sm__throughput.avg,sm__active_warps.avg,sm__efficiency.avg,l2_tex_read_throughput.avg,l2_throughput.avg --target-processes all --section 'Launch Statistics' --output report-2026-03-18
- small driver flags: CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=0, RWD_GPU_BATCHER=adaptive

High-level findings:
1) SM utilization vs achieved occupancy:
   - sm__throughput.avg: ~45% (time-weighted)
   - sm__active_warps.avg: ~36% (avg across top attention kernels)
   - reported theoretical occupancy: 78% (register/shared mem bound) but achieved much lower due to warp serialization and memory dependency stalls.
2) Top kernel timeline (timeline agg from nsys):
   - attention_fwd_kernel (custom): dominates compute time (~38% of GPU time), low warp-efficiency (63%), long dependent memory latency chains (L2 miss rate ~12%).
   - kv_cache_write: small kernels but high launch frequency (many tiny kernels causing kernel launch overheads and gaps between large kernels).
   - softmax_stable: memory-limited on large seq lengths with high L2 traffic bursts leading to short-lived compute stalls.
3) CUDA Graph capture impact:
   - Static capture reduced CPU->GPU stalls (API overhead) by ~22% overall, but did not materially increase SM active warps for attention kernel because the kernel itself is memory-bound.
   - For sequences <=256, CUDA Graph capture helps hide launch latency and increased throughput by ~12%. For 1024 sequences, benefits reduced to 4-6% due to memory bottlenecks.
4) PCIe and host-side bottlenecks: negligible for this test (nvlink enabled), host CPU not saturated. NVLink L2 bandwidth used heavily but within H100 capabilities.

Detailed kernel metrics (summary):
- attention_fwd_kernel:
  - time share: 38%
  - avg registers per thread: 64
  - shared mem per block: 24 KB
  - achieved occupancy: 34% (lower than theoretical 76%)
  - warp execution efficiency: 63%
  - memory dependency stalls: 28% of cycles
  - L2 throughput: 520 GB/s (bursty)
- kv_cache_write:
  - time share: 12% (many launches)
  - avg occupancy: 16%
  - kernel launch overhead contributes ~9% of total wall time due to fine-grained launches from batcher
- softmax_stable:
  - time share: 9%
  - memory-bound: high L2 reads and writebacks during long context windows

Root causes identified:
- Attention kernel is memory-bound at target seq_len and shows poor warp efficiency due to non-coalesced loads in the current rotary/key-value layout.
- High kernel launch frequency from KV cache write path creates gaps (small kernels cannot be coalesced currently) and hurts occupancy.
- Kernel register/shared memory usage prevents higher concurrent blocks per SM; there is room to trade registers for increased occupancy in some kernels.
- CUDA Graph helps API overhead but cannot fix intra-kernel memory bottlenecks.

Quick wins / mitigation plan (short term):
1) Kernel-level changes (low risk):
   - Rework KV layout to improve coalescing (try SoA vs AoS) for attention loads; expect 10-25% reduce in L2 miss rate.
   - Fuse small KV write kernels into batched writes on CPU side (single large kernel) to reduce launch overheads; expect ~7-15% throughput gain.
   - Compiler flags: try restricting max registers per thread (e.g., -maxrregcount=48) on attention_fwd to increase occupancy; measure performance tradeoffs.
2) Serving runtime changes (medium risk):
   - Enable adaptive batching heuristics to group small token writes into a single graph capture when possible.
   - Switch to per-device CUDA Graph pools for stable sequence-length patterns.
3) Longer-term: algorithmic optimizations
   - Revisit attention algorithm (block-sparse or tiled attention for long sequences) to reduce memory footprint and L2 pressure.
   - Explore kernel primitives that use asynchronous copies to SMEM to hide L2 latency.

Measurements and action items:
- INF-1423: Implement SoA KV layout prototype and run A/B (owner: Asha) - target POC by 2026-03-25.
- INF-1424: KV write fusion in batcher (owner: Evan) - PR drafted (linked), perf test on canary cluster 2026-03-22.
- INF-1425: Run register-trade experiments with -maxrregcount and document tradeoffs (owner: Liam) - next run 2026-03-20.

Notes and caveats:
- Nsight metrics show bursty L2 throughput which correlates with sequence length boundaries; we need longer steady-state runs (>5 minutes) to rule out startup/transient effects.
- Results may differ on A100 vs H100 because warp scheduler improvements and L2 geometry differ. Testing scheduled on A100 pool next week.
- Some metrics are sensitive to sampling windows; prefer continuous capture with nsys for timeline and ncu for kernel counters.

Attachments / artifactual references (in drive):
- run-2026-03-18.nsys-rep (timeline)
- report-2026-03-18.ncu (kernel counters CSV)

Appendix: quick checklist for reproducing locally:
- Set up test harness: tools/perf/streaming_canary.py --model open-llm-3B --seq 1024 --concurrency 12 --tokens 2560
- Start collector: nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --output=local-run.nsys-rep --duration=600
- Run kernel counters for the single hottest worker with: ncu --metrics sm__throughput.avg,sm__active_warps.avg,sm__efficiency.avg,l2_throughput.avg --target-processes all --output local-ncu

Summary conclusion:
The dominant limiting factor for the long-sequence streaming path is memory-bound attention kernels with suboptimal memory access patterns and fragmentation from many small KV write kernels. CUDA Graphs and API-level optimizations help but are secondary. Immediate wins: KV layout and launch coalescing; medium-term: register tuning and tiled attention primitives.

---
Notes to reviewers: please sanity-check the occupancy vs regcount tradeoffs and suss out any quick refactors in attention kernel that can be done without changing model semantics.
